headline: Discord Webhooks Tutorial: Send Automated Messages with Code
summary: Learn to send rich, formatted messages to Discord channels using Node.js, Python, or cURL without building a full bot.
details: This guide shows how to create a Discord Webhook URL and use simple code snippets in Node.js, Python, or cURL to send automated messages to your Discord server.
You can automate updates, server logs, or custom alerts directly to a Discord channel. This method bypasses the need to create a full Discord bot, making it a quick and efficient solution.

To set up a webhook, right-click your desired Discord channel, navigate to Integrations > Webhooks, and create a new webhook. Name it, optionally add an avatar, and copy the webhook URL. Keep this URL secure, as anyone with it can post to your channel.

Sending basic text messages is straightforward. Use a JSON payload with a 'content' field. For example, using cURL: `curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"content": "Hello from my terminal!"}' YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL`.

For more visually appealing messages, Discord webhooks support 'Embeds'. These allow you to add titles, descriptions, colors, fields, and even timestamps to your messages by including an 'embeds' array in your JSON payload.
An example embed payload includes fields like 'title', 'description', 'color' (as an integer hex code), and 'timestamp'. This allows for structured and informative notifications.

If your messages aren't appearing, Discord provides error codes: 400 Bad Request for JSON formatting issues, 404 Not Found for incorrect URLs, and 429 Too Many Requests if you hit the rate limit (5 requests per 2 seconds).
To help debug your payloads, you can temporarily use WebhookCatch.com. This free tool inspects the raw JSON your script generates, ensuring it matches Discord's expected format before sending.

headline_marked: Grand Theft Auto 6 [[locked to 30 FPS]] at launch on consoles, PS5 Pro uncertain
headline: Grand Theft Auto 6 locked to 30 FPS at launch on consoles, PS5 Pro uncertain
summary: Rockstar leadership confirmed the upcoming title will not target 60 FPS at launch, with performance modes for later updates or PC still unconfirmed.
details: Grand Theft Auto VI will launch with a 30 FPS frame rate cap on consoles, according to Rockstar North's Head of Development Rob Nelson. During a gameplay showcase, Nelson stated the game currently runs at 30 FPS and that discussions about performance modes for 60 FPS at launch or later are ongoing.

This 30 FPS target at launch has been standard for Rockstar games for over a decade, with titles like GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 receiving 60 FPS patches post-release on more powerful hardware. It's speculated that the game's complex systems, including high NPC density, dynamic weather, and advanced AI, contribute to this limitation.

While the GPU is reportedly not the bottleneck, the CPU may struggle to maintain higher frame rates. This raises questions about the PS5 Pro's capabilities, with speculation that it might not achieve 60 FPS even with its enhanced power. Rockstar has remained tight-lipped about resolution targets across consoles.

The gameplay reveal, captured on a base PS5, showcased upscaled 4K resolution from 1440p, with significant use of motion blur to enhance the perception of smoothness. It is unlikely that motion blur can be disabled on consoles, and a 40 FPS mode might be a potential compromise for VRR displays.
